newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - REED-ELSEVIER, WOLTERS SEEN AHEAD IN 96.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - REED-ELSEVIER, WOLTERS SEEN AHEAD IN 96.

text.p: Business publishers Reed
Elsevier and Wolters Kluwer are
expected to report higher 1996 earnings this week.
Analysts polled by Reuters expect Reed Elsevier to announce
a pre-tax profit on Wednesday of some 814 mln sterling on
average, versus 723 mln in 1995.
On Friday Wolters Kluwer is expected to turn in a net profit
of about 480 mln guilders versus 441 mln in 1995.
Analysts said both companies' underlying business
performance had been good but acquisitions and disposals would
distort the year-on-year comparison somewhat.
As part of a planned withdrawal from consumer publishing,
Reed Elsevier sold newspaper operations in late 1995 which
contributed over 60 mln sterling to operating profits that year.
Analysts said the proceeds of the sale had cut interest
charges, but they added this had not been enough to offset the
loss of the newspapers' contribution to earnings.
Ab Barneveld of Generale Bank said the sale of the
newspapers -- much less profitable than the group's business and
science publications -- would contribute to an improvement in
the operating margin to around 25 percent from 23.1 in 1995.
Andre Moons of ING Barings said legal publishing and U.S.
database unit Lexis-Nexis had driven a satisfactory overall
underlying business performance in 1996, although publications
for the travel industry had shown some weakness.
Barneveld said he expected Reed Elsevier's earnings
expressed in guilders to benefit strongly in 1997 from the
recent apreciation of the dollar and sterling, noting that some
70 percent of group sales were generated in these currencies.
He sees pre-tax profits rising to 940 mln sterling in 1997
and said the currency effect was probably not fully reflected
yet in the price of Elsevier's shares, which he rates a Buy.
Moons expects Reed Elsevier to post a combined pre-tax
profit of 864 mln sterling in 1997 and rates the shares a Hold.
He agrees that earnings growth will look more impressive in
guilders but believes that sterling's appreciation will impact
negatively on Reed's share price in London and that this could
in turn hold back the price of Elsevier's shares in Amsterdam.
Growth of Wolters Kluwer's bottom-line earnings for 1996
will be held back by an amortisation charge of some 60 mln
guilders stemming from its acquisition of U.S. tax publisher CCH
at the beginning of 1996.
But analysts said underlying earnings would show growth well
ahead of the company's own long-term target of 15 percent.
The amortisation charges will be recurrent but their
negative effect in the year-on-year earnings comparison is
limited to 1996 and they do not represent a real cash outflow.
Analysts said the integration of CCH and the gradual raising
of its operating margins appeared to be proceeding well and they
were also encouraged that Wolters Kluwer had made several
smaller acquisitions since the CCH buy.
Some noted that Wolters Kluwer appeared to have been more
successful than Reed Elsevier in finding profitable reinvestment
opportunities for its substantial cash flow.
ING's Moons is enthusiastic about the earnings leverage
created by its financing of the CCH buy with borrowed funds.
Moons expects Wolters to post a 1996 net profit of 482 mln
guilders, rising to 579 mln in 1997. He rates the shares a Buy.
Barneveld sees net earnings of 485 mln guilders in 1996 and
570 mln in 1997. He says Wolters Kluwer is a "great company" but
believes its high-earnings growth is well reflected in the
current price of the shares, which he rates a Hold.
